angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 31,306,500 km at 606.06 pc = 0.69 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Anderson & Francis (2012), Astronomy Letters 38, 331 (XHIP), Hipparcos astrometry, HIP 26311: the Hipparcos parallax (van Leeuwen 2007) the radius is computed with, 1.65 +/- 0.45 mas, inverted (https://doi.org/10.1134/S1063773712050015): 606.061 +/- 165.289 pc; Gaia DR3 cannot see the star
radiusSource: Radius 45 +/- 13 solar radii from Computed here, not printed by a paper: 45 +/- 13 solar radii, from the limb-darkened angular diameter 0.69 +/- 0.04 mas of Hanbury Brown, Davis & Allen (1974), MNRAS 167, 121 (the Narrabri intensity interferometer; Code, Davis, Bless & Hanbury Brown (1976), ApJ 203, 417, Table 1, and the JMDC) and the Hipparcos parallax 1.65 +/- 0.45 mas (van Leeuwen 2007, XHIP) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/167.1.121): 31,306,500 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 24820 +/- 920 K from Code, Davis, Bless & Hanbury Brown (1976), ApJ 203, 417, HD 37128: effective temperature 24820 +/- 920 K (Table 6), from the measured angular diameter and the star's flux from the ultraviolet to the infrared (https://doi.org/10.1086/154093). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Code, Davis, Bless & Hanbury Brown (1976), ApJ 203, 417, HD 37128: effective temperature 24820 +/- 920 K (Table 6), from the measured angular diameter and the star's flux from the ultraviolet to the infrared (https://doi.org/10.1086/154093)
surfaceGravitySource: log g 2.89 from 2024A&A...687A.228D; the 3 published values span log g 2.85 to 3, across which the limb law changes by at most 2.3% of the centre brightness (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A%26A...687A.228D)
spectralTypeSource: SIMBAD, * eps Ori: spectral type B0Ia (2024A&A...690A.176N)
objectTypeSource: SIMBAD, * eps Ori: main object type s*b, Blue Supergiant
projectedRotationSpeedSource: SIMBAD, * eps Ori: projected rotation speed 52 km/s, the measurement SIMBAD prefers (2024A&A...687A.228D)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's measured spectrum (Kharitonov, Tereshchenko & Knyazeva (1988), Spectrophotometric Catalogue of Stars (Alma-Ata), record 381) (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
